summary: Implemented LLM token usage tracking and budget controls with spending alerts
reason_for_change: No token usage tracking existed. Builds could exhaust API costs without limits. No visibility into spending patterns.
implementation_details: 1. Created backend/core/ai_usage.py with: (a) MODEL_COSTS for cost calculation per model, (b) DEFAULT_DAILY_BUDGETS by plan tier, (c) BudgetExceeded exception class, (d) get_user_budget() for daily usage, (e) check_budget() for pre-call validation, (f) track_usage() for recording usage, (g) calculate_cost() for USD conversion, (h) get_spending_dashboard() for admin. 2. Modified BaseAgent to accept user_id/build_id and inject budget check before LLM calls. 3. Added /analytics/spending endpoint for admin dashboard.
architecture_impact: New ai_usage collection for token tracking. Agents now require user context for budget enforcement.
security_impact: Prevents cost exhaustion attacks. Users cannot make unlimited LLM calls.
performance_impact: Minimal - one database write per build. Budget check is O(1) via Redis aggregation.
database_impact: New ai_usage and spending_alerts collections. TTL indexes recommended for 90-day retention.
backward_compatibility: Fully backward compatible - budget check skipped if user_id not provided.
migration_requirements: Create ai_usage and spending_alerts indexes. Set up TTL for 90-day data retention.
evidence: backend/core/ai_usage.py contains track_usage, check_budget, calculate_cost. BaseAgent.__init__ accepts user_id and build_id. /analytics/spending endpoint exists.
known_risks: Token counting is estimated (~1 token per 4 chars). Actual API may differ slightly from estimated costs.
rollback_plan: Remove ai_usage.py and revert BaseAgent changes. LLM calls proceed without budget checks.
